long_biography.plain_text:
Peter Lewis wanted contemporary art to challenge the people working in his insurance business. He began assembling Progressive's collection for its headquarters, choosing work intended to provoke debate among employees. Art became part of everyday office life, with photographs, prints and drawings displayed in the workplace.

His interest in creativity also shaped his giving to Princeton, where he had studied public and international affairs. He endowed the Lewis Center for the Arts and funded a library designed by Frank Gehry. A separate gift established the Lewis-Sigler Institute for Integrative Genomics, commemorating his college roommate, the biologist Paul Sigler.
